arguments.summary: A credential compromise occurred on host WS-FIN-AP01 after a phishing email triggered execution of encoded PowerShell from Outlook.exe. This led to the download and execution of a malicious DLL via rundll32.exe from the user's Temp directory, establishing C2 communication over HTTPS to 198.51.100.23. The initial reconnaissance originated from external IP 185.220.101.42, which previously conducted an Nmap scan against an internal IT host. Despite sandboxing tools flagging low risk, behavioral indicators confirmed malicious activity including host file modification and beaconing. A full EPP scan identified a low-severity PUP but missed the core payload.

arguments.rule_content:
title: Suspicious PowerShell Execution from Office Application
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\outlook.exe'
    Image|endswith: '\powershell.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: '-enc'
  condition: selection
level: high
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566.001/
description: Detects encoded PowerShell launched directly from Outlook, commonly seen in phishing payloads.

rule Suspicious_Rundll32_Temp_Load {
    meta:
        description = "Detects rundll32 loading DLLs from user Temp directories"
        author = "SOC Team"
        reference = "MITRE T1218.011"
        tlp = "amber"
    strings:
        $s1 = "\\Temp\\" nocase
        $s2 = "rundll32.exe" nocase
    condition:
        $s2 and $s1
}
